item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create a clear, friendly educational animation explaining why we hear echoes. A person stands at the left facing a distant large cliff at the right in a simple bright landscape. In one continuous wide shot, the person calls out; luminous curved sound-wave pulses travel from their mouth to the cliff, visibly bounce off the cliff, and return to the person's ear. Keep the outgoing and returning paths visually distinct using blue outgoing waves and orange reflected waves with arrowheads. Simple polished 2D classroom animation, uncluttered composition, readable visual cause and effect. Synchronize warm clear English narration: 'We hear echoes when sound bounces off distant surfaces and returns to our ears.' Quiet background, no music. Show the title 'Why We Hear Echoes' at the top and the short label 'Sound reflects' near the cliff. Complete the wave's round trip within five seconds.
